selected_concern: Duplicate != equivalent: an ArchGuard duplicate-detection hit between two call sites' verdict parsers is structurally real, but duplication alone doesn't tell you whether to merge, and merging the wrong pair (one that's intentionally-divergent) would be a mistake. The investigation step must come first and must be explicit about what it did and didn't check.
selected_slice: Having confirmed the parsing ALGORITHM (not the caller orchestration) is domain-agnostic — 'parse a judge's raw stdout into a three-state verdict, fail closed if unreadable' doesn't care whether the domain is fidelity or sufficiency, the legal-value strings are DATA not logic — sink exactly that shared algorithm into a new kernel module packages/quay/src/kernel/verdict-parse.ts exporting a generic parseBinaryVerdict(stdout, exitCode, positive, negative). The two original functions (parseFidelityVerdict, parseSemanticSufficiencyVerdict) become thin wrappers that call the kernel function, keeping their own name/signature/return type and zero caller changes — the caller-side orchestration differences (sync/uncached vs async/runAsync/2-sample-agreement/cache) are explicitly NOT touched, because ownership-first's own principle is that orchestration can legitimately stay where it is even when the underlying computation is unified.
why_now: Third real goal-branch pilot, smallest scope yet (exactly one duplicate pair), chosen specifically to test whether the ownership-first method generalizes to a 'is this duplication real or just superficially similar' judgment call, not just to mechanical literal-convergence (GOAL-031) or new-layer-introduction (GOAL-030).
why_not_others: Explicitly not expanded to any of the other ~27 dispersed-literal files a prior architecture review had already found for other verdict-shaped types (GateVerdictKind/DimensionState/ScopedGateVerdict) — that is a separate, larger, independent gap, deliberately out of scope here. Also explicitly not changing the two call sites' orchestration logic, since conflating 'the parsing is the same' with 'the orchestration should also be the same' would be exactly the kind of over-generalization the investigation was there to prevent.
risk: If the equivalence conclusion is wrong (the two really are intentionally-divergent and only superficially similar), merging them would silently couple two things that should vary independently in the future.

non_goals: do not touch any other verdict type (GateVerdictKind/DimensionState/ScopedGateVerdict and the other dispersed literals an earlier architecture review found)
do not touch the packages/quay/src directory-cycle issue

do not change criterionFidelityVerdict/sampleSemanticSufficiency's orchestration (sync/async, caching, 2-sample agreement) — only swap what they internally call, not their own signature or call pattern
do not restart any production driver process to make the new code 'take effect' — that's a separate human decision
stop_signals: same structural signals as GOAL-030/031 (code-identity falsified, production contamination, isolation failure)
interference with the concurrently-running gap-routine-quota-* tasks (different branches/worktrees, zero Touches overlap expected)
need to add a layers.yml edge

acceptance_evidence: Three ACs (AC-347..349), three-state exit codes. AC-348 requires an ArchGuard before/after pair showing the duplicate group disappears and the canonical-definition count for this parsing logic goes from 2 to 1, PLUS a negative control proving both call chains genuinely changed what they call (not just moved the file).
leakage_markers: canonical-definition count for this parsing logic goes from 2 to 1

granularity_rationale.why_not_broader: The ~27 other dispersed-literal files for OTHER verdict types (a separate, independently-discovered, larger gap) are explicitly out of scope -- folding them in would turn a one-pair merge into an open-ended vocabulary-unification project with a different risk profile and no shared acceptance evidence.
granularity_rationale.why_not_finer: Converging only ONE of the two call sites would not clear the ArchGuard duplicate-detection finding at all -- the minimal unit that actually resolves the finding is both sides converging on one shared implementation; anything smaller leaves the original signal unresolved, so there is no smaller slice that is still a complete answer.
harnessable_subproblems: caller-orchestration left unchanged, verified by each caller's PRE-EXISTING regression tests (no new test design needed)
investigation_required_subproblems: whether the two parsers are semantically equivalent or intentionally-divergent -- not decidable by the duplicate-detection tool itself; required reading both function bodies and their own self-documenting comments before any slice could be chosen
primitives_reused: the kernel-module-as-sink-layer pattern established in GOAL-030

timeline.note: This case is the clearest T0/T1 example in the corpus: the v1 input already carried an investigation conclusion under a T0 cutoff, which is exactly the hindsight mismatch the redesign removes.

expected_concerns: a duplicate implementation of one concept exists across the packages/plugin boundary and has no single owner
the equivalence question is unresolved, so any merge is premature

stage_b_reference.investigate_or_goal_rationale: The equivalence investigation is COMPLETE as of T1, so 'investigate' would re-do finished work. Note the trap the v1 benchmark fell into: it labelled this 'goal' while feeding a T0 state, which made 'investigate' look wrong for the right reason.
stage_b_reference.minimum_sufficiency_rationale: Converging only one of the two call sites does not clear the duplicate-detection finding at all — the minimal unit that resolves the signal is both sides sharing one implementation. Nothing smaller is still a complete answer; nothing larger is needed because the callers' orchestration legitimately differs and the other verdict types are a separate, larger gap.
stage_b_reference.reference_slice: Having confirmed the parsing ALGORITHM (not the caller orchestration) is domain-agnostic — 'parse a judge's raw stdout into a three-state verdict, fail closed if unreadable' doesn't care whether the domain is fidelity or sufficiency, the legal-value strings are DATA not logic — sink exactly that shared algorithm into a new kernel module packages/quay/src/kernel/verdict-parse.ts exporting a generic parseBinaryVerdict(stdout, exitCode, positive, negative). The two original functions (parseFidelityVerdict, parseSemanticSufficiencyVerdict) become thin wrappers that call the kernel function, keeping their own name/signature/return type and zero caller changes — the caller-side orchestration differences (sync/uncached vs async/runAsync/2-sample-agreement/cache) are explicitly NOT touched, because ownership-first's own principle is that orchestration can legitimately stay where it is even when the underlying computation is unified.
alternative_valid_slices: Sink the shared algorithm and keep both callers unchanged (the selected approach) — zero caller churn.
Sink the algorithm AND unify the two callers' orchestration — rejected: over-generalises, the orchestration difference is intentional.
Leave the duplication and record it as an accepted cross-tree exemption — defensible only if the two were intentionally divergent, which T1 rules out.
adjacent_reasonable_slices: The ~27 dispersed literal files for other verdict types (a separate, larger gap)
clearly_too_broad: Unify all verdict-shaped types in one pass
Merge the two callers' orchestration as well as the parser
Touch the packages/ directory-cycle issue in the same goal
clearly_too_fragmented: Convert only one of the two call sites
Add a shared helper without making either original function delegate to it
stage_b_reference.expected_delta_predicted_at_t1: the duplicate-detection group disappears and the canonical definition count for this algorithm drops to one, with both call chains confirmed to have actually changed what they call
stage_b_reference.expected_delta_observed: Duplicate group cleared; canonical-definition count for the shared algorithm 2 -> 1; both call chains independently verified to delegate.
